claims.text: The initial FeNiCoCrCu nanoparticles are an equiatomic, homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Incremental Mn substitution alters the alloy's effective mixing enthalpy while preserving its initial solid-solution state.
Mn substitution increases the effective mixing enthalpy.
A critical effective-mixing-enthalpy threshold relative to configurational entropy governs retention of the single-phase solid solution.
Below the critical threshold, configurational entropy is sufficient to stabilize a single-phase solid solution from 473 to 1923 K.
Above the critical threshold, the free-energy minimum shifts in favor of phase separation and secondary-phase formation at high temperature.
Nanoparticles with low or minimal Mn substitution have lower effective mixing enthalpy than nanoparticles with higher Mn content.
Nanoparticles with low or minimal Mn substitution will retain a single-phase solid solution throughout thermal cycling from 473 to 1923 K.
Nanoparticles with higher Mn content will form secondary phases during thermal cycling from 473 to 1923 K.
Secondary-phase formation will produce split or emerging XRD peaks.
Secondary-phase formation will produce exothermic signals in DSC scans.
The critical mixing-enthalpy threshold may depend on nanoparticle size, minor compositional heterogeneity, and experimental conditions.
Oxidation or additional surface effects could independently drive phase separation.
